attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, written in his own voice. He is not quoting or paraphrasing anyone else.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both qualifiers, 'on its own' and 'as far as I know', and keeps the examples of original work. It is an observation limited by what Marcus knew on 2024-06-05.

contract.note: The contract keeps the knowledge qualifier instead of reading the line as an absolute claim that GPT-4 had done no such work. That is fair to Marcus's words. Scoring it would need evidence of what he knew at the time, which no public capability record can provide.

evidence.note: This is the source statement itself, dated 2024-06-05. It shows the wording and the qualifier. It cannot prove itself or show what Marcus knew.

reviews.rationale: The claim only says what Marcus knew of at publication. Evidence about what GPT-4 could do cannot confirm or refute it. Only contemporaneous proof of his awareness could. The packet has none, and that kind of evidence is not realistically testable, so the claim is not adjudicable. It is not a broken case.
